questions.text: Describe how your electronic circuit achieves its intended function — what happens electrically from input to output?
What electronic components are central to your mechanism, and what role does each play?
What signal or energy transformation does your circuit perform?
Which part of your circuit is most critical to achieving the intended function, and why?
What provides the energy or power for your design to operate?
Do you know of any electrical requirements your design depends on (such as voltage, current, frequency, or similar constraints)? If not, what information would you need to determine them?
Are there any known electrical constraints that your design must stay within to function correctly?
What does your electronic design specifically NOT do or NOT handle?
At what point does your electronic design stop and another system or component begin?
What external systems, components, or interfaces does your design depend on to function?

rule_nuances.description: Inventor must identify the physical operating principle of their electronic mechanism, not merely name components
If the invention involves energy conversion or power delivery, the inventor must acknowledge the power source and energy budget
Inventor must not define the mechanism exclusively by platform or product name. The underlying principle must be stated.

covered_areas: Concept-level explanation of basic circuit function and electronic mechanism
Concept-level power delivery and energy budget awareness
Concept-level rationale for selecting electronic components
Electronic mechanism completeness as a reasoning quality assessment
not_covered_areas: Regulatory approval and certification (CE, FCC, UL)
PCB layout and manufacturing design rules
Firmware and embedded software logic — outside the authority of the current parent electronics pack and requires separate governance authorization.
Safety certification (IEC 61508, ISO 26262) — concept-level risk awareness may be authorized separately
known_limitations: Early-concept stage only — not suitable for production-ready designs
Parent domain covers electronics broadly; sub-domain depth requires child pack
Questions are calibrated for parent-domain concept validation and may not satisfy specialist-level engineering review without a child domain pack.

This coverage declaration defines Stage 2 parent-domain reasoning authority only. It does not authorize Stage 3 implementation readiness, Stage 4 engineering readiness, or Stage 5 prototype readiness.
Coverage does not imply ability to validate, certify, simulate, or produce build-ready designs.

claims.fact: For a resistive element, the voltage across it equals the current through it multiplied by its resistance (Ohm's law). The DOE handbook writes this relationship as E = I × R, using E for voltage; it is presented here with V for voltage (notation normalization only, same relationship).
claims.limitation: Bounded resistive / Ohm's-law reference relationship only. InventorAI does not determine that the inventor's device, component or circuit is ohmic or that this relationship applies to the inventor's design. No project-specific calculation.

claims.fact: Basic electrical power equals voltage multiplied by current (basic DC / reference form). The DOE handbook writes this relationship as P = I × E (P = IE), using E for voltage; it is presented here with V for voltage (notation normalization only, same relationship).
claims.limitation: Basic DC / reference relationship only. Not extended to AC power factor, reactive or apparent power, efficiency, thermal rating, power-supply, battery or motor sizing, component rating, safety or any project-specific calculation.

claims.relationship: voltage: V; current: A; resistance: Ω; power: W
claims.fact: SI units: electric potential difference / voltage — volt (V); electric current — ampere (A); electric resistance — ohm (Ω); power — watt (W).
claims.limitation: Unit discipline only. Correct units do not validate a circuit or design.

claims.relationship: E = P × t (constant P throughout t)
claims.fact: Power is the rate at which energy is transferred or used. When the power P remains constant throughout the stated duration t, the energy transferred E equals P multiplied by t (E = P × t), where E is the energy transferred, P the constant power and t the duration. The DOE handbook supplies the factual definition of power as a rate of energy transfer / use; E = P × t is InventorAI's own algebraic restatement of that definition under the explicit constant-power restriction, not an equation quoted verbatim from DOE.
claims.limitation: Constant-power reference relationship only. InventorAI does not establish that power is constant or that this relationship applies to the inventor's invention, and never infers constant power from inventor text, classification signals, component names or a project value. No varying-power treatment, average-power substitution, integration formula, efficiency assumption, battery capacity / runtime, charging, rating, sizing, safety assessment or project-specific calculation.

claims.relationship: energy: J; power: W; duration: s; J = W · s
claims.fact: SI units: energy — joule (J); power — watt (W), expressed as joules per second (W = J/s); duration (time) — second (s). The corresponding unit relationship is J = W · s.
claims.limitation: Unit discipline only (reference text). J and s are not added as units, quantities, bindings or methods of the shared deterministic calculation / units owner; no conversion factor or other quantity is presented. Correct units do not validate a design.

_governance_notes.electrical_td_slice1_reference_fundament: Electrical / Electronics Technical Deepening Slice 1 — Basic Electrical Reference Fundamentals (Owner-authorized bounded reference fundamentals): reference_fundamentals is ONE additive, declaration-only group (basic_electrical_reference_v1, applicable gap PHYSICAL_FEASIBILITY) recording three bounded reference claims with exact source provenance (electronics_electrical:PR004–PR005), source-use-policy provenance (electronics_electrical:PR006–PR007) and explicit limitations. It is inert for the classifier, get_active_rules, Path-N question serving, NeedRouting, progression, readiness, evidence state and the domain registry loader (no loader or schema change); it is not a classification or substance signal and carries no executable formula selection, user-input variable, calculation procedure, threshold or applicability logic. Its only consumer is the presentation layer's bounded gap-scoped CAP-01 context (web/cap01_guidance.py, catalogue copy in web/ui_text.py), which shows the same bounded reference set only while the exact canonical PHYSICAL_FEASIBILITY gap is OPEN or PARTIAL and never selects which relationship applies to a project. It does not change the domain-level CAP-01 checklist / research profile (CAP01_ELECTRONICS_INTERFACE_V1). Existing provenance electronics_electrical:PR001–PR003 are unchanged, and IEC 60050 / IPC-2221B (PR001 / PR002) are not the claim authority for these reference fundamentals.
_governance_notes.electrical_energy_time_reference_fundame: Electrical / Electronics — Energy-Time Reference Fundamentals (ELECTRICAL-ENERGY-TIME-REFERENCE-01; Owner-authorized bounded extension of the Stage 18 / CAP-01 reference fundamentals): reference_fundamentals gains ONE further additive, declaration-only group (electrical_energy_time_reference_v1, applicable gap PHYSICAL_FEASIBILITY) recording exactly two bounded reference claims — constant_power_energy_reference (E = P × t, ONLY when P remains constant throughout t; InventorAI's algebraic restatement of the DOE definition of power as an energy transfer / use rate) and energy_time_unit_discipline (J, W, s; J = W · s) — with exact source provenance (electronics_electrical:PR008–PR009), source-use-policy provenance (electronics_electrical:PR010–PR011) and explicit limitations. The existing group basic_electrical_reference_v1 and its claims, sources and wording are unchanged and render first. Same inertness as that group: inert for the classifier, get_active_rules, Path-N question serving, NeedRouting, progression, readiness, evidence state and the domain registry loader (no loader or schema change); no classification or substance signal, executable formula selection, user-input variable, calculation procedure, threshold or applicability logic; nothing is added to the shared deterministic calculation / units owner. Its only consumer is the same bounded gap-scoped CAP-01 presentation (exact canonical PHYSICAL_FEASIBILITY gap OPEN or PARTIAL). No charge / current / time, coulomb, Ah / Wh, battery capacity, runtime, charging, chemistry, rating, sizing or safety content. Existing provenance electronics_electrical:PR001–PR007 are unchanged.
